FLASHCARD SET · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

First Concepts flashcards.

Eleven cards about how the world works: big and small, up and down, open and closed, full and empty, one and many — plus the posting game that puts a toy in, then takes it all out again. These are action words and size words — the cards work best when your toddler's whole body gets involved.

These cards belong to Toddler 2 on the Kiddo School learning path.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Act out every card

    These are doing words as much as looking words: stretch UP, curl DOWN, arms WIDE for big. The body remembers what the hands do.

  2. 02

    Say the pair together

    Show big, then small — back to back. Opposites teach each other; one card makes the other make sense.

  3. 03

    Hunt the concept at home

    After the full card, find a full cup and an empty one. Every card has a matching object somewhere in your house — the house is the second deck.

  4. 04

    Follow the energy

    Some days the body cards (up, down, open) are the hit; other days the thinking ones (one, many) land. Let your toddler lead.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Big Flashcard for Toddlers

      Big is the first size word most toddlers learn, usually applied to everything larger than themselves — cars, dogs, Daddy. The giant star on this card makes the idea unmistakable.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Starts the size vocabulary with a word your child will shout for years.

      Play it in a minute

      Hand over the biggest orange from the fruit bowl and announce it grandly.

      What kids learn from it

      Comparing two objects and picking the larger on sight.

      How to print it

      Print large, fittingly, and let the margins breathe.

      Grown-up tip

      Big only works next to something small, so keep pairs handy.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Big lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Small Flashcard for Toddlers

      Small is the opposite card: tiny, little, just-right-for-small-hands. Toddlers adore small things they can hold, which gives this card a built-in fan club.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Adds the other end of size; the word for precious, pocket-sized things.

      Play it in a minute

      Hunt the hallway for the smallest thing you can balance on a palm.

      What kids learn from it

      Sharp eyes for the tiniest details on shelves and pavements.

      How to print it

      Shrink it down on the page, just to make the point.

      Grown-up tip

      Pocket finds stay out of mouths; small is a big word too.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Small lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Up Flashcard for Toddlers

      Up is the direction your toddler has been requesting since they could point — up to be lifted, up to the shelf, up up UP. The arrow on the card points the way your toddler already knows by heart.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Attaches a word to the lift your child requests roughly hourly.

      Play it in a minute

      Bounce a balloon off the ceiling and call up as it rises.

      What kids learn from it

      Direction words that match the body's own movements.

      How to print it

      A single sheet does it; this word travels lightly.

      Grown-up tip

      Spend it generously on lifts and swings; cooperation comes back as interest.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Up lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Down Flashcard for Toddlers

      Down is where the ball goes, where the slide goes, where everything dropped ends up. Paired with up, this card gives you a complete game of arms high, arms low — the cheapest fun in the house.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Explains where dropped things go, complete with the word to announce them.

      Play it in a minute

      Drop pegs into a saucepan and call down for every clatter.

      What kids learn from it

      Cause and effect narrated with a single satisfying word.

      How to print it

      Print two; one for the kitchen, one for wherever dropping happens.

      Grown-up tip

      Gravity is the co-teacher here; you just supply the commentary.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Down lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Open Flashcard for Toddlers

      Open is the word for every door, lid and box your toddler wants inside. The open book on the card is an everyday kind of magic: open means ready to start.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Names the everyday magic trick that lids and flaps perform.

      Play it in a minute

      Open the curtains together each morning with a flourish and the word.

      What kids learn from it

      Action words for hands, spoken at the exact moment they happen.

      How to print it

      Laminating survives sticky fingers, if your machine is feeling generous.

      Grown-up tip

      Designate one low drawer as forever openable; it saves every other one.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Open lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Closed Flashcard for Toddlers

      Closed is open's other half — shut doors, closed lids, folded hands. The pair teaches the pair: neither word quite makes sense without the other one next to it.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Hands over the word for finished, shut, done; the lid back on the day.

      Play it in a minute

      Snap the lunchbox lid and say the word at the exact moment it catches.

      What kids learn from it

      That every word like this keeps an opposite in its pocket.

      How to print it

      Standard paper is fine; this one lives by the front door.

      Grown-up tip

      The click of a tin or zip does half the teaching.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Closed lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Full Flashcard for Toddlers

      Full means filled right up to the top — the glass that cannot take another drop. It is a word your toddler sees at every meal, which makes it one of the easiest concepts to teach for free.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Names the cup that cannot take another drop; a state your family knows.

      Play it in a minute

      Fill a mixing bowl with clementines until nothing else fits, then stop and admire.

      What kids learn from it

      Quantity words that describe a state, not a count.

      How to print it

      Colour optional; this one shares a page with empty quite happily.

      Grown-up tip

      One deliberate overflow for comedy, then stop at the brim next time.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Full lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Empty Flashcard for Toddlers

      Empty is full's shadow — the cup after the drink, the box after the toys, the plate after dinner. Toddlers find empty mildly alarming at first, then deeply satisfying.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Celebrates the finished bowl and the tin scraped clean, a small triumph.

      Play it in a minute

      Tip the clementines out slowly until the mixing bowl stands bare.

      What kids learn from it

      Noticing absence, a genuinely abstract idea made visible.

      How to print it

      Keep it beside the full card; the pair does the teaching.

      Grown-up tip

      The word lands best right after the last item leaves the bowl.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Empty lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      One Flashcard for Toddlers

      One is where counting starts: one biscuit, one shoe, one you. The card shows a single bright ball — no crowd, no confusion, just one.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Turns everyday single objects into a very first number worth naming.

      Play it in a minute

      Hold up one shoe, then bring out its twin, and feel the difference.

      What kids learn from it

      One-to-one correspondence, the quiet root of all later maths.

      How to print it

      Print one copy only, fittingly.

      Grown-up tip

      Name single things as you pass; a doorbell, a moon, a plug.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the One lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      Many Flashcard for Toddlers

      Many is one's opposite: lots, a crowd, a whole handful. The card is packed with balls, and the fun is in the contrast — one finger for one ball, both hands wide for many.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Covers every pile too big to count with one generous word.

      Play it in a minute

      Gather every ball in the house into one corner; that is many.

      What kids learn from it

      Rough quantity; lots versus one, without any numbers yet.

      How to print it

      Run off as many copies as you fancy; the card would approve.

      Grown-up tip

      Resist counting on their behalf; many is many, and that is enough.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Many lesson on the Learning Path.

      FLASHCARD · FIRST CONCEPTS · AGES 18–24 MONTHS

      In Flashcard for Toddlers

      In is the word for inside — the block in the box, the hand in the mitten, the toddler in the bath. It is one of the first position words toddlers use correctly, usually while posting things into slots.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card plants

      Names where everything disappears to; sleeves, pockets, the recycling drawer.

      Play it in a minute

      Park a peg inside an empty mug and let small fingers retrieve it.

      What kids learn from it

      Spatial words that organise the whole world of containers.

      How to print it

      Small enough for a pocket copy; print one of those too.

      Grown-up tip

      Mugs, pockets, sleeve cuffs; the whole house is full of ins.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the In lesson on the Learning Path.
